gate_contract: test-model, test-model-extended, test-integration, and test-chaos fail unless every named test ran and passed (scripts/run-named-tests.sh)
fault_schedule: seeded: SIGKILL of a partition leader, a follower, or the group coordinator; SIGSTOP 2 s; isolation of a broker's peer links; a one-way peer cut (requests dropped, replies lost); a 200 ms peer delay. Each fault is healed and every broker is ready again before the next. Separately: disk full and sync failure through the storage fault adapter; a flood of 400 producers, 200 slow-header clients, and a storm of 600 fetches; a lost produce reply; a dead-broker route.

acceptance.OP-01: malformed, duplicate-key, oversized, bad-base64, path-traversal, and wrong-topology peer and client requests are rejected before any backend sees them
acceptance.OP-02: a locked data dir, wrong node, changed topology bytes, unformatted dir, or non-loopback listener without the opt-in all fail to start, and the manifest is unchanged
acceptance.OP-03: flood: 400/400 acknowledged, peak 25 pending waiters (cap 256); slow headers closed after 5 s while metadata keeps being served; the fetch storm answers 200, 429, or 503 within the deadline; disk full and sync failure fail closed with STORAGE_ERROR and outcome unknown
acceptance.OP-04: a lost reply is resent with the same identity and lands once at the same offsets; a stale route reaches the new leader within one pass of at most 3 requests per call; no client goroutine leak
acceptance.OP-05: two full chaos runs on the final code acknowledged 11,224 and 11,306 records with no violations: no loss, no duplicates, identical committed replicas, both groups processed every record, disjoint assignments, monotonic committed offsets
acceptance.OP-06: SIGTERM exits 0 within its bound; data survives the restart; logs and metrics carry no payload; readyz is false before the listeners and after shutdown
acceptance.FR_INV: every FR-01 to FR-08 and INV-01 to INV-12 maps to an executed test in docs/traceability.md

metrics_summary.batches_of_100: RF1 6,423-12,482 records/s; RF3 2,518-3,788 records/s; leader CPU 140-330%
metrics_summary.read_back: 11,353-35,803 records/s; 10.8-14.0 segment and index comparisons per fetch
metrics_summary.cold_restart_s: 4.5-7.4 for small logs; 35-167 for 0.5-1.4 GiB per partition

defects_found_and_fixed: M6: a new RF3 coordinator never started serving (failover messages left unsent)
M3: the leader's sent-RPC table was unbounded under message loss
M3: every proposal re-sent all pending entries (no flow control)
M4: followers one round trip behind a busy leader were evicted from the ISR
M3: a rejected higher-term vote reset election timers, so a stale candidate kept a partition leaderless
M3: restart replay and single-entry reads were quadratic
M4: operation and gate history were never pruned; writes stopped after about 4,096 operations
M7 recovery: up to three copies of the replayed prefix in memory
write outcome after a storage failure reported not_applied instead of unknown
mutation_checks: PR 1: 6, PR 2: 6, PR 3: 12, PR 5: 3; all killed
output_location: full logs under .test-output/ on the test host, uploaded as CI artifacts for the chaos job; scrubbed benchmark results in docs/benchmarks/
limitations: No TLS or authentication; peers are trusted (X4). Non-loopback listeners need --allow-insecure-bind.
No group commit, binary payload, or snapshots: single-record throughput is fsync-bound, and restart time and memory grow with the log (X2/X3).
Fetch does not long-poll; read barriers are not batched.
Chaos applies one fault at a time; overlapping faults are not scheduled.
The SIGKILL tests do not prove power-loss durability; that depends on the platform's fsync (ADR-007).
Delivery to consumers is at least once.
